findings.title: Raw signup body, including plaintext password, is logged before validation
findings.explanation: req.body is passed to the logger unfiltered, so the user's plaintext password and email (PII) are written to logs. The claim that the logger already redacts sensitive fields is risky here: redaction usually matches known key names/paths, and this payload is unvalidated, so clients can send unexpected shapes or misnamed fields (e.g. 'pass', 'pwd', nested objects, arrays, a string body) that bypass redaction. Failed signups are exactly the cases where users mistype or send odd payloads, so the leak is most likely in the very data being captured. Logs are typically retained, shipped to third parties, and widely accessible, which creates GDPR/SOC2/PCI exposure and credential-compromise risk. Remove this line, or log only a safe allowlist (e.g. key names present, types, lengths, and a boolean per field), never values.

findings.title: Logging is placed before validation, so it records attacker-controlled arbitrary data
findings.explanation: Unauthenticated endpoint: anyone can send arbitrarily large or crafted bodies that get written to logs in full. This enables log flooding/cost inflation, log injection, and storage of junk or malicious content. If logging is needed, do it on validation failure only, with size limits and an allowlist.

findings.title: Better approach: log structured validation errors instead of the payload
findings.explanation: The actual need is knowing why validation fails. Use signupSchema.safeParse(req.body) and on failure log result.error.issues (paths and codes/messages, which do not contain the submitted values by default for most issues) and return a 400 with details. Currently signupSchema.parse throws a ZodError, and unless there is error-handling middleware that maps it to a 400, failures may surface as 500s. This gives the debugging signal without storing sensitive input.

findings.title: Redaction assumption is unverified and untested
findings.explanation: The PR relies on the logger's redaction without showing its configuration or adding a test. If redaction is kept as defense in depth, add a test asserting that a signup body with password (and variants) is not emitted in log output, and document which keys are redacted.

findings.title: Log level and message
findings.explanation: info level for every signup attempt adds volume in production. If you keep any logging, use debug or log only failures at warn, and include a request ID/correlation ID rather than user data so failures can be traced.
